restoration_note: The teaching has two clear movements: (a) the fivefold integrity of the natural — none of the five degrees can be missing or the whole collapses, and what the self produces in the flesh today is humbled because it cannot match the height/breadth/length/depth of the elevated states and is finally swallowed up in the great sea of natural perception; (b) the Lord makes five things known to the rational — kind-of-the-light, how aeons and darkness exist, how the light shames the power of darkness, that the soul has come to the boundary of death-in-the-flesh and is brought out by the upper gate, and that the self's coverings of the Good are bound at last. The second half (5222–5236) consists almost entirely of editor letter-completions and ordinal restorations (ⲡϣⲁⲣⲧ̄, ⲡⲙ̄ⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲡⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ, Ⲧ̄Ⲧⲙⲁⲍϥⲧⲁⲩ, Ⲧ̄Ⲧⲙⲁⲍϯⲟⲩ) that are highly constrained by the visible parts of the words and by the parallel ordinal-formula structure; these are all confident. Section 5231's ⲥⲱⲙⲁ ('body, which is the flesh') is a clean four-character fit with strong corpus parallels. The genuinely damaged stretches are 5208's middle (ⲛⲧⲥⲁⲣⲝ̄ ___ ___ ___ ⲙⲡⲟⲟⲩⲉ ⲍⲓⲝⲛ ⲛⲍⲟ ⲙⲡⲕⲁⲍ ___) where the participial verb of 'rising up today' cannot be securely fixed, 5209's prepositional phrase '___ forth from ___-ⲗⲉ which exceeds' (the noun ending in -ⲗⲉ is unrecoverable), 5211's 3-char tail after 'mountains', and 5216–5217's stretch about how the productions are gathered into a single sea and swallowed in some manner — the verb at {19}+ⲟⲩⲁⲡ and the partial-ⲭⲟⲟ word at {22} are not constrained by the lexicon or by the visible surroundings.

Noun ending in -ⲗⲉ that 'exceeds'; the lexicon yields no certain match.
